generated_texts:
TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data transfer between devices over IP networks.
What is the main difference between TCP and UDP? The main difference between TCP and UDP is that TCP is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data transfer, while UDP is a connectionless protocol that prioritizes speed over reliability.
What is the purpose of the three-way handshake in TCP? The three-way handshake is used to establish a connection between two devices, ensuring that both devices are ready to communicate and that the connection is reliable.
What is the difference between a TCP segment and a TCP packet? A TCP segment refers to the data and headers transmitted over a TCP connection, while a TCP packet is a more general term that can refer to any packet transmitted over a network, including those using other protocols.
What is the purpose of the ACK flag in TCP? The ACK flag is used to acknowledge receipt of data, allowing the sender to confirm that the data was received correctly and to retransmit any lost or corrupted data.
What is the purpose of the SYN flag in TCP? The SYN flag is used to initiate a connection, allowing the sender to request a connection and the receiver to respond with an acknowledgement.
What is the purpose of the FIN flag in TCP? The FIN flag is used to terminate a connection, allowing the sender to indicate that it has finished sending data and the receiver to confirm that the connection is closed.
What is the difference between a TCP connection and a UDP connection? A TCP connection is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data transfer, while a UDP connection is a connectionless protocol that prioritizes speed over reliability.
What is the purpose of the sequence number in TCP? The sequence number is used to keep track of the order in which data is transmitted, allowing the receiver to reassemble the data in the correct order and to detect any lost or corrupted data.
What is the purpose of the window size in TCP? The window size is used to control the amount of data that can be transmitted before an acknowledgement is required, allowing the sender to adjust the amount of data transmitted based on the receiver's ability to process it.
